elements.text: Power Tool Safety Rules

elements.label: text
elements.text: Read and understand the tool manual and these instructions for the use of this table with your router. Failure to follow all instructions listed below may result in serious personal injury.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: SAVE THESE INSTRUCTIONS

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Work Area

elements.label: text
elements.text: Keep your work area clean and well lit. Cluttered benches and dark areas invite accidents.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Do not operate power tools in explosive atmospheres, such as in the presence of flammable liquids, gases, or dust. Power tools create sparks which may ignite the dust or fumes.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Keep bystanders, children, and visitors away while operating a power tool. Distractions can cause you to lose control.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Electrical Safety

elements.label: text
elements.text: Grounded tools must be plugged into an outlet properly installed and grounded in accordance with all codes and ordinances. Never remove the grounding prong or modify the plug in any way. Do not use any adaptor plugs. Check with a qualified electrician if you are in doubt as to whether the outlet is properly grounded. If the tools should electrically malfunction or break down, grounding provides a low resistance path to carry electricity away from the user. Improper grounding can shock, burn, or electrocute. Grounded tools are equipped with threeconductor cord and three-prong type plugs. Before plugging in the tool, be certain the outlet voltage supplied is within the voltage marked on the nameplate. Do not use "AC only" rated tools with a DC power supply.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Double-insulated tools are equipped with a polarized plug (one blade is wider than the other.) This plug will fit in a polarized outlet only one way. If the plug does not fit fully in the outlet, reverse the plug. If it still does not fit, contact a qualified electrician to install a polarized outlet. Do not change the plug in any way. Double Insulation eliminates the need for the three-wire grounded power cord and grounded power supply system. Before plugging in the tool, be certain the outlet voltage supplied is within the voltage marked on the nameplate. Do not use "AC only" rated tools with a DC power supply.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Avoid body contact with grounded surfaces such as pipes, radiators, ranges and refrigerators. There is an increased risk of electric shock if your body is grounded. If operating the power tool in damp locations is unavoidable, a Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter must be used to supply the power to your tool. Electrician's rubber gloves and footwear will further enhance your personal safety.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Don't expose power tools to rain or wet conditions. Water entering a power tool will increase the risk of electric shock.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Do not abuse the cord. Never use the cord to carry the tools or pull the plug from an outlet. Keep cord away from heat, oil, sharp edges, or moving parts. Replace damaged cords immediately. Damaged cords increase the risk of electric shock.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When operating a power tool outside, use an outdoor extension cord marked "W-A" or "W." These cords are rated for outdoor use and reduce the risk of electric shock. Refer to "Important Information About Extension Cords" in your router table manual.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Personal Safety

elements.label: text
elements.text: Stay alert, watch what you are doing and use common sense when operating a power tool. Do not use tool while tired or under the influence of drugs, alcohol, or medication. Amoment of inattention while operating power tools may result in serious personal injury.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Keep guards in place. Maintain the guards in working order and in proper adjustment and alignment.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Avoid accidental starting. Be sure switch is "OFF" before plugging in. Carrying tools with your finger on the switch or plugging in tools that have the switch "ON" invites accidents.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Remove adjusting keys or wrenches before turning the tool "ON." A wrench or a key that is left attached to a rotating part of the tool may result in personal injury.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Do not overreach. Keep proper footing and balance at all times. Proper footing and balance enable better control of the tool in unexpected situations.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Use safety goggles (head protection). Wear safety goggles (must comply with ANSI Standard Z87.1) at all times. Wear non-slip footwear and a hard hat, if appropriate. Also, use face or dust mask if cutting operation is dusty and ear protectors (plugs or muffs) during extended periods of operation.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Tool Use and Care

elements.label: text
elements.text: Use clamps or other practical way to secure and support the workpiece to a stable platform. Holding the work by hand or against your body is unstable and may lead to loss of control.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Do not force tool. Use the correct tool for your application. The correct tool will do the job better and safer at the rate for which it is designed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Do not use tool if switch does not turn it "ON" or "OFF." Any tool that cannot be controlled with the switch is dangerous and must be repaired.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Disconnect the plug from the power source before making any adjustments, changing accessories, or storing the tool. Such preventive safety measures reduce the risk of starting the tool accidentally.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Keep guards in place. Maintain the guards in working order and in proper adjustment and alignment.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Store idle tools out of reach of children and other untrained persons. Tools are dangerous in the hands of untrained users.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Never leave tools running unattended. Turn the power OFF. DO NOT leave tool until it comes to a complete stop.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Maintain tools with care. Keep cutting tools sharp and clean. Properly maintained tools, with sharp cutting edges are less likely to bind and are easier to control. Any alteration or modification is a misuse and may result in a dangerous condition.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Check for damaged guards or parts, misalignment or binding of moving parts, breakage of parts, and any other condition that may affect the tool's operation. If damaged, have the tool properly repaired or replaced before using. Many accidents are caused by poorly maintained tools. Develop a periodic maintenance schedule for your tool.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Use only accessories that are recommended by the manufacturer for your model. Accessories that may be suitable for one tool may become hazardous when used on another tool.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Service

elements.label: text
elements.text: Tool service must be performed only by qualified repair personnel. Service or maintenance performed by unqualified personnel could result in a risk of injury. For example: internal wires may be misplaced or pinched; safety guard return springs may be improperly mounted.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When servicing a tool, use only identical replacement parts. Use of unauthorized parts or failure to follow maintenance instructions may create a risk of electric shock or injury. Certain cleaning agents such as gasoline, carbon tetrachloride, and ammonia may damage plastic parts.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Additional Safety Warnings for Router Tables

elements.label: text
elements.text: Read and understand table and router manual and accessory warnings. Failure to follow all instructions and warnings may result in serious personal injury.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Fully assemble and tighten all fasteners required for this table and for mounting the router to the plate. Do not use the router table until all assembly and installation steps have been completed. Check the table and the router to make sure fasteners are still tight before each use. A loose table is unstable and may shift in use.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Make certain the router is not plugged into a power outlet when installing into the table, removing from table, making adjustments or changing accessories. Router could accidentally start.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Do not plug router motor power cord into standard wall outlet. It must be plugged into the router table switch. Power tool switches and controls need to be within your reach in emergency situations.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Before operating, make sure the entire unit (table with router installed) is placed on and secured to a solid, flat, level surface and will not tip. Use of auxiliary in-feed and out-feed supports is necessary for long or wide workpieces. Long workpieces without adequate support can flip off the table or cause the table to tip over.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Be certain router motor is fully and securely clamped in the router base. Periodically check the base fastener clamping tightness. Router motor can vibrate loose from the base during use and fall from table.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Do not use the router table without the overhead guard or auxiliary bit guard. Remove all dust, chips, and any other foreign particles that can affect its function. Adjust the guard height so that it clears the router bit and the workpiece. The guard will aid in keeping hands from unintended contact with rotating bit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Never place your fingers near a spinning bit or under the guard when router is plugged in. Never hold the workpiece on the out-feed side of bit. Pressing the workpiece against the out-feed side of the fence may cause material binding and possible kickback pulling hand back into bit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Guide workpiece by the fence to maintain control of workpiece. Do not place material between router bit and fence while routing the edge. This placement will cause the material to become wedged, making kickback possible.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Routers are intended for working with wood, woodlike products and plastic or laminates, not for cutting or shaping metals. Be sure workpiece does not contain nails, etc. Cutting nails may cause loss of control.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Do not use bits that have a cutting diameter that exceeds the clearance hole in the tabletop insert. Bit could contact insert ring, throwing fragments.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Install bit in accordance with instructions in router manual and securely clamp the router bit in the collet chuck before making any cuts to avoid bit becoming loose during operation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Never use dull or damaged bits. Sharp bits must be handled with care. Damaged bits can snap during use. Dull bits require more force to push the workpiece, possibly causing the bit to break or the material to kick back.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The router table is designed to cut flat, straight and squared materials. Do not cut material that is warped, wobbly, or otherwise unstable. If the material is slightly curved but otherwise stable, cut the material with the concave side against the table or fence. Cutting the material with the concave side up or away from table may cause the warped or wobbly material to roll and kick backm causing user to lose control.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Never start the tool when the bit is engaged in the material. The bit cutting edge may grab the material, causing loss of control of the workpiece.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Feed the workpiece against the rotation of the bit. The bit rotates counterclockwise as viewed from the top of table. Feeding the work in the wrong direction will cause the workpiece to "climb" up on the bit, pulling the workpiece and possibly your hands into the rotating bit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Use push sticks, vertical and horizontally mounted featherboards (spring sticks), and other jigs to hold down the workpiece. Push sticks, featherboards, and jigs eliminate the need to hold the workpiece near the spinning bit.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Additional Safety Warnings for Router Tables

elements.label: text
elements.text: Piloted bits along with the starter pin are used when routing internal and external contours on the workpiece. Use the auxiliary bit guard when shaping material with the starter pin and piloted bits. The starter pin and bearing of the piloted bit assist in maintaining control of the workpiece.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Do not use the table as a workbench or work surface. Using it for purposes other than routing may cause damage and make it unsafe to use in routing.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: "Climb-cutting" - The bit must not enter the workpiece in the same direction as the feed direction, which is likely to cause the workpiece to "climb" and may lead to loss of control during operation (Fig. B).

elements.label: text
elements.text: "Fence Traps": One type of improper fence location warrants special attention. "Fence traps" happen when the fence is positioned so far back that the front side (power switch side) of the workpiece would be behind the router bit.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Important Information About Extension Cords

elements.label: text
elements.text: If an extension cord is necessary, a cord with adequate size conductors that is capable of carrying the current necessary for your tool must be used. This will prevent excessive voltage drop, loss of power or overheating. Grounded tools must use 3-wire extension cords that have 3-prong plugs and receptacles.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: The smaller the gauge number, the heavier the cord.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: The mounting holes for the left and right panels are spaced so that the panel will only fit on the correct end of the back. Before attaching the panels, make sure that the predrilled holes for the hinges and door catch are on the INSIDE surface of the panel.

elements.label: list_item

elements.label: list_item

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Align the holes in the base with the holes in the sides and back, and attach using five Allen-head connector screws (38) (Fig. 2).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Tighten all fasteners securely with the 4mm hex key (43). The screw head should be in the counterbore, below the panel surface. DO NOT OVERTIGHTEN!

elements.text: ATTACHING THE SWITCH TO THE TABLETOP (Fig. 3)

elements.label: text
elements.text: Assembly Hint: It may be easier to attach the switch bracket if you stand the tabletop on its back edge for this step.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Align the two holes in the switch mounting bracket (15) with the two through-holes in the router tabletop. From the top side of the table, insert two #10-32 x 1 1 /2″ pan-head machine screws (34) through the tabletop and bracket and secure the bracket in place with two small washers (30) and two #10-32 KEPS nuts (29) (Fig. 3).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Insert two #10-32 KEPS nuts (29) into the hex-shaped recesses in the back of the switch assembly (14) with the toothed washer facing away from the recess. Secure the switch to the switch mounting bracket with two #10-32 x 1/2″ pan-head machine screws (33) while holding the KEPS nuts in place in the recess with your finger.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: ATTACH THE TABLETOP (Fig. 4)

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: The tabletop may be shipped with the miter channel in place. To access the tabletop mounting holes, remove the channel for this step.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.With the base assembly upright, position the tabletop (1) on the base assembly, making sure the switch is in the front, as shown in Fig. 4.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Secure the tabletop to the base with four Allen-head connector screws (38).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Tighten all fasteners securely with the 4mm hex key. The screw head should be in the counterbore, below the panel surface. DO NOT OVERTIGHTEN!

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: ASSEMBLE THE ALUMINUMMITER CHANNEL TO THE TABLETOP (Fig. 5)

elements.label: text
elements.text: Assembly Hint: It may be easier to install the miter channel if you lay the table on its back for this step.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Center the miter channel (2) in the slot on the tabletop; then press the miter channel into the slot.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.From the top side of the tabletop (1), insert three #10-32 x 7/8″ countersunk Phillips machine screws (36) through the holes in the miter channel (2) and the tabletop (Fig. 5).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Secure with a small washer (30) and a #10-32 KEPS nut (29) on each screw.

elements.text: ATTACH THE DOOR (Figs. 6 and 7)

elements.label: text
elements.text: HINT: Applying bar soap or bees wax to the screw threads will make them easier to install into the panels.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.With the bumps on the catch plate against the door surface, attach the metal catch plate (13B) to the inside of the narrow end of the door with a 5/8″ lg. flat-head Phillips wood screw (35). The edge of the catch plate should be even with the edge of the door (Fig. 6).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Attach the door hinges (12) to the left side panel with two 5/8″ lg. flat-head Phillips wood screws (35) on each hinge (Fig. 7).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Attach the magnetic catch (13A) to the inside of the right side panel using two 5/8″ lg. flat-head Phillips wood screws (35) (Fig. 7).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.Slowly open and close the door, making sure that it moves freely and does not rub on the base or top, does not come in contact with the switch assembly, and that it latches correctly.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: If the door rubs, make sure the side panels and switch are assembled correctly.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: If the magnetic catch does not contact the catch plate, loosen the screws on the magnetic catch and reposition it using the slotted holes in the catch.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Insert the pins molded into the top of the vacuum port (18) into the holes on the rear of the aluminum fence (16), as shown in Fig. 8.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.From the underside of the fence, insert two #10-32 x 5/8″ countersunk machine screws (37) up through the holes in the bottom of the fence and vacuum port. Secure in place with two #10-32 KEPS nuts (29) (Fig. 8).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Place the fence right-side-up on a flat surface and align the counterbored holes in the fence facings (17) with the slotted holes in the fence. The counterbored side of the facings should face OUT (Fig. 9).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.Attach both fence facings (17) to the front of the fence, using two 1/4-20 x 1″ carriage bolts (39) and two large clamping knobs (19) for each fence facing (Fig. 9).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 5.From the front of the overhead guard (20), insert two 1/4-20 x 1 1 /2″ carriage bolts (40) through the holes in the guard. Slide a spacer (21) on each bolt so that the tabs on the spacers fit into the slots on the guard.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 6.From the front of the fence, insert the carriage bolts through the holes in the top center of the fence. The tabs on the spacers will fit into the top channel on the fence. Secure in place with a small clamping knob (22) on each bolt (Fig. 9).

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: To simplify installation of the router adapter plate and router, do not install the fence onto the router table at this time.

elements.label: text

elements.text: ATTACH ROUTER TO MOUNTING PLATE (Figs. 11 and 12)

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Remove the plastic subbase from your router (Fig. 11).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: If your router has its own dust extraction hood that mounts to the top of the metal router base and you want to use it under the router table, this is a convenient time to install it.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Using Chart 1, determine the hardware and mount type for your router.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: For most router models, the screws are driven into threaded holes in the router's base (mount type 1).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: For some router models, the screws go all the way through the base and are fastened with washers and nuts (mount type 2).

elements.label: text
elements.text: The top and front of the mounting plate is determined by the location of the guide pin holes. These holes are to the right of the bit opening.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.Refer to the mounting plate guide (Fig. 10) on page 14 and align the appropriate mounting plate holes for your router to the router base holes. Make sure that the depth adjustment controls on the router face the front of the mounting plate.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 5.Mount your router to the mounting plate (Fig. 12).

elements.text: If the fence is already installed on the table, remove it before proceeding.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Place the router mounting plate (3) in the opening so the numbers on the scales are right side up, as seen from the front of the table. Using a straight edge, check to be certain that the surface of the router mounting plate is flush with the tabletop surface. NOTE: Failure to make sure the router mounting plate is flush with the tabletop surface can result in poor routing performance. Slide a square cut board from right to left across the router mounting plate to be sure that it moves smoothly.

elements.label: list_item

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: TO REMOVE THE ROUTER AND/OR ROUTER MOUNTING PLATE

elements.label: text
elements.text: To remove the router from the mounting plate, you must first remove the router mounting plate from the router table.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: THE FENCE MUST BE REMOVED FROM THE ROUTER TABLE WHEN REMOVING OR REINSTALLING THE ROUTER MOUNTING PLATE.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Make sure that the router is NOT plugged into a power outlet when installing into the table, removing from table, making adjustments or changing accessories. Router could accidentally start.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: OVER-TABLE HEIGHT ADJUSTMENT

elements.label: text
elements.text: The router adapter plate features an access hole to allow use with the over-table height adjustment feature on the Bosch 1617 series routers. Refer to your router manual for additional information on using this feature.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For the Porter Cable 892 and 895 and the Milwaukee 5615 and 5616 model routers, it is necessary to drill an access hole to accommodate the over-table height adjustment:

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Remove the subbase from the router and align the mounting holes in the subbase with the corresponding mounting holes in the adapter plate. Be sure to orient the subbase so that the router switch will be toward the front of the table.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.Secure the router mounting plate (3) to the table with four #10-32 x 1/2″ pan-head machine screws (33) (Fig. 13) through the outermost corner holes in the plate. Tighten the screws snugly, but do not overtighten.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Loosen the four #10-32 x 1/2″ pan-head Phillips machine screws (33) holding the router mounting plate to the tabletop.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Lift the router mounting plate and router upwards from the tabletop.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Remove the countersunk machine screws securing the router to the mounting plate.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.When reinstalling the router mounting plate, be sure that the plate is level with the tabletop. If needed, readjust as described above.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Using a pencil or centerpunch, mark the location of the over-table height adjustment hole on the router adapter plate.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Remove the subbase from the adapter plate and carefully drill the over-table height adjustment hole.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.Make sure that the hole will accommodate the height adjustment tool for your router. Remove any burrs or rough edges with sandpaper.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.From underneath, slide two 1/4-20 x 1 3 /4″ carriage bolts (41) up through the holes in the bottom of the fence. Slide a large washer (31) onto each bolt and loosely attach a large clamping knob (19) onto each bolt.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Insert the carriage bolt heads through the holes of the J-slots on the tabletop, making sure the bolt head is below the inside surface of the tabletop and can slide freely into the J-slot.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Slide the fence assembly left and into the J-slot and

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: make sure that it slides smoothly from front to back. when aligning the fence for routing operations. Once

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: Use the scale on the tabletop as a guide the fence is positioned and aligned correctly, tighten the clamping knobs SECURELY.

elements.label: text
elements.text: THE ROUTER TABLE MUST BE SECURED TO A STABLE WORK SURFACE WHENEVER IT IS IN USE. FAILURE TO DO SO COULD CAUSE IT TO TIP OR SHIFT UNEXPECTEDLY.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Preferred method:

elements.label: text
elements.text: The base of the router table has four mounting holes. These holes can be used to attach it to a workbench or work surface with four 1/4″ wood screws and washers or bolts, washers, and nuts (not provided).

elements.label: text
elements.text: HINT: Position the router table in the desired location and mark the hole locations using the holes in the table base. Then drill suitable pilot (for wood screws) or through-holes (for bolts).

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Alternative method:

elements.label: text
elements.text: The base can be secured to a workbench or work surface with C-clamps.

elements.label: section_header

elements.label: text
elements.text: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THAT THE ROUTER IS TURNED OFF AND THE POWER CORD IS UNPLUGGED BEFORE MAKING ANY ADJUSTMENTS.

elements.text: 2″ in diameter (10), for use with bits with diameters up to 1 7 /8″

elements.text: 2 3 /4″ in diameter (11), for use with bits with diameters up to 2 5 /8″

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: TO INSTALL TABLETOP INSERTS (Fig. 16):

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Select the tabletop insert that best accommodates the router bit to be used.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Press the insert into the large hole in the router mounting plate (Fig. 16). If the fence is in the way, loosen the clamping knobs on the fence and slide the fence back out of the way.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Press down evenly over the tabs until the insert locks into place.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.To remove, pull up gently until the tabs disengage. When not in use, store tabletop inserts in a resealable plastic bag in the router table cabinet.

elements.label: text
elements.text: DO NOT attempt to remove tabletop inserts from the tabletop unless the router is unplugged.

elements.text: A 14-gauge (or heavier) three-wire extension cord with a three-hole grounding receptacle and three-hole grounding plug is to be used for connecting the switch to an electrical outlet.

elements.text: DAMAGED OR WORN EXTENSION CORDS ARE NOT TO BE USED AND ARE TO BE REPLACED IMMEDIATELY.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The electrical cord at the back of the switch will accept three-hole extension cords.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The electrical receptacles at the back of the switch will accept either three-prong or two-prong plugs from a router or accessory.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In the event of a malfunction or breakdown, grounding provides the path of least resistance for electrical current in order to reduce the risk of electrical shock. This switch box is equipped with an electrical cord that has an equipment-grounding connector and a grounding plug.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The extension cord must be plugged into a matching outlet that has been installed by a licensed electrician and grounded in accordance with all local codes and ordinances.

elements.label: text
elements.text: DO NOT modify the plug from the switch if it does not plug into the extension cord. Obtain an extension cord with the proper outlet.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Improper connection of the equipment-grounding conductor can result in risk of an electrical shock.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The conductor with insulation that has a green outer surface, with or without yellow stripes, is the equipmentgrounding conductor.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: DO NOT CONNECT THE EQUIPMENT-GROUNDING CONDUCTOR TO A LIVE TERMINAL.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Check with a licensed electrician if the grounding instructions are not completely understood, or if there is doubt as to whether the electrical outlet or extension cord is properly grounded.

elements.label: text
elements.text: DO NOT PERMIT FINGERS TO TOUCH TERMINALS OF THE PLUG WHEN PLUGGING IT INTO OR REMOVING IT FROM THE OUTLET.

elements.label: text
elements.text: IF NOT PROPERLY GROUNDED, A POWER TOOL CAN PRESENT POTENTIAL HAZARDS OF ELECTRICAL SHOCK, WHICH CAN POSSIBLY RESULT IN SERIOUS BODILY INJURY OR DEATH, particularly when used in a damp location, in proximity to plumbing, or out-of-doors. If an electrical shock occurs, there is always the potential of a secondary hazard, such as your hands contacting the router bit, or falling down or against an object.

elements.label: text
elements.text: USE THE SWITCH BOX ONLY WHEN PROPERLY ASSEMBLED TO THE ROUTER TABLE. USE ONLY WITH A ROUTER THAT HAS ALSO BEEN PROPERLY INSTALLED ON A PROPERLY ASSEMBLED ROUTER TABLE.

elements.label: text
elements.text: THE SWITCH HAS A RATING OF 15 AMPS. DO NOT EXCEED A TOTAL COMBINED RATING OF 15 AMPS WHEN CONNECTING THE ROUTER AND ANY ACCESSORIES SUCH AS A LIGHT OR WET/DRY VACUUM.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: CONNECTING THE ROUTER POWER CORD TO THE SWITCH

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: MAKE SURE THAT THE SWITCH POWER CORD IS NOT PLUGGED INTO ANY ELECTRICAL OUTLET AT THIS TIME. IF IT IS, UNPLUG IT.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: MAKE SURE THAT ROUTER SWITCH IS IN THE OFF POSITION.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Plug the router power cord into one of the electrical outlets on the back of the switch case.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Form the excess power cord into a coil.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Wrap two pieces of friction tape or cable ties around the coiled cord at opposite sides of the coil.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.Allow some slack so that the cord does not become stretched when it is plugged into the switch box outlets.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: If desired, at this time plug the power cord from an accessory, such as a wet/dry vac or light, into the other outlet on the back of the switch case.

elements.label: text
elements.text: MAKE SURE THAT POWER CORDS FROM THE ROUTER, ACCESSORIES, THE SWITCH CASE, AND THE EXTENSION CORD DO NOT AND CANNOT COME IN CONTACT WITH THE ROUTER OR ANY MOVING PARTS OF THE ROUTER.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: This switch has a 15 amp rating and is intended only for turning the router and connected accessories such as a wet/dry vacuum "ON" and "OFF".

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: GENERAL INFORMATION

elements.label: text
elements.text: The power switch is designed for use with most BOSCH Router Tables. It provides the convenience of an ON (RESET)-OFF switch at the front of the table, thus eliminating the need to reach underneath the table to turn the router ON and OFF.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The power switch also provides an optional simultaneous ON-OFF control of an additional accessory, such as a light or wet/dry vac. The switch has an internal, resettable circuit breaker to provide overload protection.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: text
elements.text: With the lockout key in place and the cover raised, the switch can be toggled to the ON (RESET) position. Note that the red slide panel is fully retracted from the switch.

elements.label: text
elements.text: With the lockout key in place and the cover raised, the switch can be toggled to the OFF position. The switch can also be turned OFF by pressing on the cover. Note that the red slide panel is fully retracted from the switch.

elements.label: text
elements.text: With the lockout key removed, the red slide panel covers the top portion of the switch, locking it in the OFF position. The switch cannot be toggled to the ON (RESET) position without first fully inserting the lockout key.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: SWITCH OPERATION

elements.label: text
elements.text: This section explains the operation and features of the switch prior to plugging the power cord into an extension cord. The intent is to familiarize the user with the switch operation without actually turning ON the router.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The switch incorporates two positive features to prevent inadvertent switching ON of the router and the unauthorized, and possibly hazardous, use by others:

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: There is a transparent cover over the actual switch to prevent the accidental switching ON of the router. This cover allows you to see a small red light on the switch toggle when the switch is turned ON. The switch can be turned OFF quickly by pushing the cover.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: The light is ON when the switch is ON.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: The light is OFF when the switch is OFF.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: The lockout key must be completely inserted into the side of the switch case before the switch can be turned ON.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: To operate the switch: MAKE SURE THAT THE EXTENSION CORD IS NOT PLUGGED INTO AN ELECTRICAL OUTLET BEFORE PROCEEDING ANY FURTHER.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Insert the lockout key into the side of the switch case. See Figure 17.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.To turn the router ON, lift the switch cover and

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: toggle switch to ON (RESET) position. See A above. Gently lower the switch cover. Letting the switch

elements.label: text
elements.text: cover drop closed may cause the switch to turn OFF.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.To turn the router OFF, press the switch cover. The switch toggle will be in the OFF position, as shown in B above.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: NEVER LEAVE THE ROUTER

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: UNATTENDED WHILE IT IS RUNNING OR BEFORE IT COMES TO A COMPLETE STOP.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.To lock switch in the OFF position, press the cover to turn the switch OFF and remove the lockout key completely from the side of the switch case. The red slide panel should cover the top half of the switch, as shown in C above.

elements.label: text
elements.text: With the lockout key removed and the red slide panel covering the top half of the switch toggle, the switch CANNOT be toggled to the ON position.

elements.label: caption
elements.text: Switch receptacle orientation (as viewed from front of switch)

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: text
elements.text: BEFORE PROCEEDING ANY FURTHER, MAKE SURE THE SWITCH ON THE ROUTER IS IN THE OFF POSITION AND THE SWITCH LEVER IS IN THE OFF POSITION.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The switch power cord can now be plugged into the extension cord.

elements.label: text
elements.text: MAKE SURE THAT POWER CORDS FROM THE ROUTER, ACCESSORIES, THE SWITCH CASE, AND THE EXTENSION CORD DO NOT AND CANNOT COME IN CONTACT WITH THE ROUTER OR ANY MOVING PARTS OF THE ROUTER.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: ROUTER AND SWITCH OPERATION

elements.label: text
elements.text: This section explains operation of the switch with the power cord plugged into the extension cord.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The router will turn ON when the toggle switch is toggled to the ON (RESET) position.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Position the ON/OFF switch on the router in the ON position. On certain routers this will require the use of the switch trigger and "LOCK-ON" button. (Consult router owner's manual.) Make sure the switch on the switch case is in the OFF position when doing this.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.To turn the router ON, lift the switch cover and toggle the switch to the ON position. See A on page 21.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.To turn the router OFF, push on the switch cover. See B on page 21.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NEVER LEAVE THE ROUTER UNATTENDED WHILE IT IS RUNNING OR BEFORE IT COMES TO A COMPLETE STOP.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: In the event of an overload, the internal switch circuit breaker will trip the switch to the OFF position. This will interrupt power to the router and any accessory plugged into the switch itself. If this

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: occurs, proceed as follows:

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Unplug the switch cord from the extension cord.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Remove the workpiece from the router table.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Correct the cause of the overload situation (i.e. the load exceeds the rated capacity of the switch).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.Plug the switch power cord into the extension cord.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 5.Restart the router as described in the section ROUTER AND SWITCH OPERATION.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: WHEN THE ROUTER TABLE IS NOT IN USE

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Press the switch cover to turn the switch OFF.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Remove the lockout key.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Store the lockout key in a safe location where it is not available to children and other unauthorized persons.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.Unplug the switch cord from the extension cord.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 5.Remove the router bit from the router.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 6.Position the router collet assembly below the top of the router table.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: If the key should become lost or damaged, replacement keys are available from your local Bosch dealer.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: ATTACHING AND USING A WET/DRY VACUUM

elements.label: text
elements.text: MAKE SURE THE SWITCH IS OFF AND UNPLUGGED BEFORE PLUGGING IN A WET/DRY VACUUM OR REACHING IN THE AREA UNDER THE TABLE OR NEAR THE ROUTER BIT!

elements.label: text
elements.text: This router table features two vacuum ports for the attachment of a wet/dry vac with a 2 1 /2″ nozzle. Select which port will provide optimal results, based on your routing operation:

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: For routing operations where shavings and dust are typically pulled down under the tabletop, such as grooving, use the slotted hole in the back of the table cabinet. This will help prevent a buildup of sawdust and wood chips in the cabinet. To attach, simply push the nozzle into the port.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: For routing operations where sawdust and wood chips are ejected onto the tabletop, such as many edge-cutting operations, use the vacuum port on the back of the fence. To attach, simply push the nozzle into the port while holding the fence assembly in place.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The vacuum can be plugged into the router table switch and the cord routed through the slot in the vacuum port on the back of the cabinet. Be sure the cord does not interfere with router operation.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: USING THE ROUTER TABLE

elements.label: text
elements.text: Operating the router table without a wet/dry vac can result in an excessive buildup of sawdust and wood chips under the fence assembly and guard, and in the cabinet, reducing the performance of the router table and fence assembly.

elements.label: text
elements.text: RECOMMENDATION: To maximize performance, regardless of whether a wet/dry vac is being used, remove the sawdust and wood chips from the cabinet and from under the fence assembly and guard as needed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: RECOMMENDATION: It is always a good practice to keep the work area clean. As necessary, remove any accumulated sawdust and wood chips from the top of the router table, as well as from the surrounding work area and floor.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: INSTALLING THE ROUTER BIT (CUTTER)

elements.label: text
elements.text: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THAT THE ROUTER IS TURNED OFF AND THE POWER CORD IS UNPLUGGED BEFORE MAKING ANY ADJUSTMENTS.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Install the router bit according to the instructions included with your router. Because of the large variation of router bits, certain router bits may not always operate in the desired manner with this router table.

elements.label: text
elements.text: To ensure that the most popular bits will perform satisfactorily, install the bit so that the router collet engages 3/4″ of the router bit shank. If the shank of the router bit bottoms out in the collet, back out the router bit approximately 1/16″ to allow for proper tightening.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NEVER INSTALL ROUTER BITS WITH LESS THAN 3/4″ OF SHANK ENGAGEMENT IN THE COLLET.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: ASSEMBLING THE FEATHERBOARDS (Figs. 18-20)

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: The top/front side of each featherboard is marked to indicate proper feed direction.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Fence Featherboard (Figs. 18 and 19)

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Insert two 1/4-20 x 1 1 /2″ carriage bolts (40) through the slotted holes in the featherboard (24). See Fig. 18.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Slide a large washer (31) onto each carriage bolt and thread a small clamping knob (22) three or four turns onto each carriage bolt.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.To install on the fence, slide a spacer (21) over the head of each carriage bolt, aligning the tabs on the spacer with the slot in the featherboard (Fig. 19). Then slide the carriage bolt heads into the T-slot on the top of the fence.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.Secure the featherboard assembly by tightening the knobs, making sure that the tabs on the spacer are in the slot on the fence.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Tabletop Featherboard (Fig. 20)

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: The featherboard slide plate assembly is T-shaped for use in the miter channel and has round indentations on the bottom for the carriage bolt heads.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Insert two 1/4-20 x 1 1 /2″ carriage bolts (40) through the holes in both the lower (25A) and upper (25B) featherboard slide plate and the slotted holes in the featherboard (24) as shown in Fig. 20.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Slide a large washer (31) onto each carriage bolt and thread a small clamping knob (22) three or four turns onto each carriage bolt.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.To install the featherboard in the miter channel, insert the featherboard slide plate into the miter channel. Then slide the featherboard to the desired location on the miter channel and tighten the clamping knobs.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: ROUTING USING FEATHERBOARDS (Fig. 21)

elements.label: text
elements.text: Featherboards are helpful in controlling the workpiece while routing and assist in keeping the workpiece flat on the tabletop. The tabletop featherboard, combined with the fence featherboard, helps keep the workpiece pressed against the fence and tabletop. The best location for the featherboards varies according to your application, workpiece size, and other factors.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Loosely install the featherboard(s) as described on page 24.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Place the workpiece on the router table so that it is squarely against the fence.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 3.Position both featherboards snugly against the workpiece and tighten the clamping knobs.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.The workpiece should move with some resistance but without requiring a great effort.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 5.For wider workpieces, the tabletop featherboard cannot be used. The second featherboard may also be positioned on the fence, if desired.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Additional featherboards, model RA1187, can be purchased from your Bosch retailer.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Featherboards are an aid in holding the workpiece in position when routing on a router table.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: They are NOT intended to hold the workpiece in place alone when the workpiece is in contact with the bit, or at any other time when the bit is turning.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: NEVER let go of the workpiece when routing using the featherboards until the cut has been completed and the workpiece is completely clear of the bit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: FOR ACCURACY IN ROUTING AND IMPROVED CONTROL, THE WORKPIECE SHOULD BE HELD AGAINST THE ROUTER TABLE FENCE WHEN ROUTING.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: ADJUSTING THE FENCE FACING (Fig. 22)

elements.label: text
elements.text: The right and left fence facings are attached to the front face of the router table fence and can be adjusted inward or outward from the router bit to allow proper clearance for different-sized bits. To provide the best support during routing operations, the fence facings should be as close to the bit as possible without being able to come in contact with the bit (typically about 1/4″ from the bit is a suitable distance).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Loosen the two clamping knobs on the backs of the fence facings and slide the facings inward or outward from the router bit as needed.

elements.label: text
elements.text: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THAT THE FENCE, FENCE FACINGS, AND GUARD CANNOT COME IN CONTACT WITH THE ROUTER BIT. FAILURE TO DO SO WILL RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE ROUTER TABLE AND CAN CAUSE PERSONAL INJURY.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Once the fence facings are in the desired position, tighten the clamping knobs SECURELY.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: ADJUSTING DEPTH AND HEIGHT OF CUT (Fig. 23)

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 1.Select a board that is smooth and straight, with good square edges.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 2.Mark lines "A" and "B" on the end of the board, as shown in Detail 23.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Line "A" indicates the desired height of cut.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Line "B" indicates the desired final depth of cut.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: The area outlined by "A," "B" and the edge of the board is the area that will be cut away.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: If the desired depth of cut can be cut in a single pass, loosen the fence clamping knobs and move the fence forward or backward until the outermost cutting edge of the router bit is aligned with line "B". It may be necessary to reposition the guard to provide clear access.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: For deeper cuts, do NOT attempt to make the cut in a single pass. Make multiple shallower cuts passes, progressively moving the fence backward until the desired depth of cut is reached.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 4.Use the scales on the table top as a guide to align the fence; then SECURELY tighten both fence clamping knobs.

elements.label: text
elements.text: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THAT THE FENCE AND GUARD CANNOT COME IN CONTACT WITH THE ROUTER BIT. FAILURE TO DO SOWILL RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE ROUTER TABLE AND CAN CAUSE PERSONAL INJURY.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 5.Following the instructions that came with your router, adjust the router height of cut until the top of the router bit lines up with line "A."

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 6.Once all adjustments have been made, double-check that:

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: The router is SECURELY tightened in the router base.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: The router bit is SECURELY tightened in the router collet, with at least 3/4″ shank engagement.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: The router base is SECURELY tightened to the router mounting plate.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 7.Remove the board from the table.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: When making adjustments, use a piece of scrap wood to make trial cuts before making the cut with the actual workpiece.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: FULL EDGE CUTTING OR JOINTING (Figs. 24 and 25)

elements.label: text
elements.text: For maximum strength and accuracy, boards that are to be joined together should be smooth and true. The edges should be true to the workpiece surface. You can true the edges using the router table with a straight bit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: Use the jointing shim(s) to provide continuous support for the workpiece as it is fed past the router bit.

elements.label: text
elements.text: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THAT THE ROUTER IS TURNED OFF AND THE POWER CORD IS UNPLUGGED BEFORE MAKING ANY ADJUSTMENTS.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Loosen the clamping knobs on the left fence facing.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Align the slot in the jointing shim(s) with the holes in the fence facing, and slide the jointing shim(s) between the fence and the left fence facing (Fig. 24).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Use one jointing shim for a 1/16″ offset, or both jointing shims for a 1/8″ offset

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Install a straight bit in the router.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Position both fence facings so that they clear the bit by 1/4″.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Tighten the four clamping knobs holding the fence facings in place.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Place a straight edge or a straight piece of wood on the table so that it rests against the left fence facing.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Move the fence back until the straight edge lines up with the cutting edge of the bit and is still in contact with the left fence facing.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Tighten the clamping knobs.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Remove the straight edge or board.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 10.Adjust the height of the bit so that it will cut the complete thickness of the workpiece.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 11.Position the featherboards, if desired. See ROUTING USING FEATHERBOARDS on page 25.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 12.Remove the board from the table and lower the overhead guard to the operating position. Tighten the guard clamping knobs SECURELY. NOTE: When making adjustments, use a piece of scrap wood to make trial cuts before making the cut with the actual workpiece.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 13.Make sure that both the router and switch box are OFF; then plug the router into the switch box.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 14.While firmly holding a piece of scrap wood against the fence and down against the router table, feed a piece of scrap wood toward the bit in the direction shown by the arrow in Fig. 25.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: 15.Using the switch box, turn the router OFF. If any adjustments are needed, unplug the power cord and repeat steps 6-11 until all adjustments are correct. Once you are satisfied with all settings, make the cut with the actual workpiece.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: EDGE CUTTING WITH NONPILOTED ROUTER BITS (Figs. 26 and 27)

elements.label: text
elements.text: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THAT THE ROUTER IS TURNED OFF AND THE POWER CORD IS UNPLUGGED BEFORE MAKING ANY ADJUSTMENTS.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: NOTE: If the jointing shim is installed, remove it before proceeding.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When using nonpiloted router bits, the fence is used to set the depth of cut. For deep cuts, do not try to cut the total depth all in one pass. Repeat the cut, taking multiple smaller cuts.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Install the desired bit in the router.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Follow the instructions on page 26 to set the desired depth of cut and height of cut (Fig. 26). Make sure that the fence and router are SECURELY in place.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Position both fence facings so that they clear the bit by 1/4″.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Tighten the four clamping knobs holding the fence facings in place.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Position the featherboards, if desired. See ROUTING USING FEATHERBOARDS on page 25.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Remove the board from the table and lower the overhead guard to the operating position. Tighten the guard clamping knobs SECURELY. NOTE: When making adjustments, use a piece of scrap wood to make trial cuts before making the cut with the actual workpiece.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Make sure that both the router and switch box are OFF; then plug the router into the switch box.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: While firmly holding a piece of scrap wood against the fence and down against the router table, feed a piece of scrap wood toward the bit in the direction shown by the arrow in Fig. 27.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Using the switch box, turn the router OFF. If any adjustments are needed, unplug the power cord and repeat steps 2-8 until all adjustments are correct. Once you are satisfied with all settings, make the cut with the actual workpiece.

elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: EDGE CUTTING WITH PILOTED ROUTER BITS (Figs. 28 and 29)

elements.label: text
elements.text: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THAT THE ROUTER IS TURNED OFF AND THE POWER CORD IS UNPLUGGED BEFORE MAKING ANY ADJUSTMENTS.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: NOTE: If the jointing shim is installed, remove it before proceeding.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Install the desired piloted bit in the router.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Follow the instructions on page 26 to set the desired height of cut (Fig. 28). Make sure that the router is SECURELY in place.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Adjust the router table fence back just enough that the pilot on the router bit will control the depth of cut. The router bit pilot should just barely protrude past the fence facings. Tighten the fence clamping knobs SECURELY.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Position both fence facings so that they clear the bit by 1/4″.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Tighten the four clamping knobs holding the fence facings in place.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Remove the board from the table and lower the overhead guard to the operating position. Tighten the guard clamping knobs SECURELY.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: When making adjustments, use a piece of scrap wood to make trial cuts before making the cut with the actual workpiece.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Make sure that both the router and switch box are OFF; then plug the router into the switch box.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: While firmly holding a piece of scrap wood against the fence and down against the router table, feed a piece of scrap wood toward the bit in the direction shown by the arrow in Fig. 29.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Using the switch box, turn the router OFF. If any adjustments are needed, unplug the power cord and repeat steps 2-8 until all adjustments are correct. Once you are satisfied with all settings, make the cut with the actual workpiece.

elements.text: Guard not shown for clarity

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: GROOVING, FLUTING, AND VEINING (Figs. 30 and 31)

elements.label: text
elements.text: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THAT THE ROUTER IS TURNED OFF AND THE POWER CORD UNPLUGGED BEFORE MAKING ANY ADJUSTMENTS.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: NOTE: If the jointing shim is installed, remove it before proceeding.

elements.label: text
elements.text: When performing these routing operations, the use of featherboards and a push shoe is recommended.

elements.label: text
elements.text: For best results and maximum accuracy, the side of the workpiece that will be against the fence must be square and straight.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If you are using a wet/dry vac, it should be connected to the vac port on the back of the table cabinet.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Install the desired end-cutting bit in the router.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Follow the instructions on page 26 to set the desired depth-of-cut (location of cut) and height-of-cut (Fig. 30). Make sure that the fence and router are SECURELY in place.

elements.label: text
elements.text: IMPORTANT: For deep cuts, do not try to cut the total depth (controlled by the router bit height) all in one pass. Repeat the cut, taking smaller cuts until the desired depth is reached.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Position both fence facings so that they provide continuous support of the workpiece.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Tighten the four clamping knobs holding the fence facings in place.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Position the featherboards, if desired. See ROUTING USING FEATHERBOARDS on page 25.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Remove the board from the table and lower the overhead guard to the operating position. Tighten the guard clamping knobs SECURELY.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: When making adjustments, use a piece of scrap wood to make trial cuts before making the cut with the actual workpiece.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Make sure that both the router and switch box are OFF, then plug the router into the switch box.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: While firmly holding a piece of scrap wood against the fence and down against the router table, feed a piece of scrap wood toward the bit in the direction shown by the arrow in Fig. 31.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Using the switch box, turn the router OFF. If any adjustments are needed, unplug the power cord and repeat steps 2-8 until all adjustments are correct. Once you are satisfied with all settings, make the cut with the actual workpiece.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Router Table Operation

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: USING THE STARTER PIN FOR EDGE FORMING OF CURVES

elements.label: text
elements.text: The starter pin (26) is used instead of the fence for operations that involve routing curves in the workpiece. It should be used only with bits that have pilot bearings. Thread the starter pin into the threaded hole in the mounting plate and tighten securely with a slotted screwdriver (Fig. 32).

elements.label: text
elements.text: Attach the starter pin guard (27) to the mounting plate by threading a #10-32 x 3/8″ truss-head machine screw (28) through the hole in the guard post and into the threaded hole in the mounting plate. Align the guard with the hole in the mounting plate so it is over the bit, and securely fasten the guard in place.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Always use the starter pin guard when routing with the starter pin.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: When using the starter pin, the feed direction of the workpiece is always right to left across the front of the bit (Fig. 33).

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Set the workpiece against the front of the starter pin and swing it slowly into the bit.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: While routing, make sure the workpiece is always in contact with the bit's pilot bearing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The auxiliary guard must be used for this type of operation. Keep fingers clear of spinning bit. Do not attempt to route small workpieces.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: USING AMITER GAUGE (not supplied)

elements.label: text
elements.text: The aluminum T-slot miter gauge slot may be used with most stationary table saw miter gauges that measure 3/4″ wide x 3/8″ deep.

elements.label: text
elements.text: NOTE: For ALL routing operations requiring the use of the miter gauge with the fence, BE SURE to align the fence using the scales on the top of the router table before making any cuts. Miters can be cut by loosening the knob on the protractor head, turning the protractor head up to 60° in either direction, and retightening the protractor head knob.
